title: Japan national CPI (January 2027), 08:30 JST
source: EST: stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/1582.html ('Consumer Price Index — Schedule of Release', page's own 'Last Update : 23 January 2026'), re-fetched raw direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 13,839 bytes) and parsed cell-by-cell out of its single 17-row HTML table by this session. Against the header 'Japan: Survey month | Date of release || Ku-area of Tokyo (preliminary): Survey month | Date of release || Remarks', the second-to-last row parses exactly as ['January, 2027', 'February 19', 'February', 'February 26', ''] — i.e. the January-2027 national CPI releases 2027-02-19, with the Tokyo February flash following 2027-02-26. The empty Remarks cell is itself evidence: this release carries no yearly or fiscal-yearly average. 2027-02-19 is a Friday and is clear of Japanese public holidays per the Cabinet Office's own list (www8.cao.go.jp/chosei/shukujitsu/syukujitsu.csv, HTTP 200, 21,538 bytes, Shift-JIS, fetched by this session the same day; the nearest 2027 holidays are 2027-02-11 and 2027-02-23). Filed estimate on three counts, identical to its sibling rows: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS: for US statistical agencies and no slot for Japan's Statistics Bureau, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and the schedule page's own last-update stamp is 2026-01-23. The 08:30 JST release time is the Statistics Bureau's standing convention and is NOT read off this page — treat it as the weaker half of this entry
notes: DISCOVERED during the japan-cpi-2027-03-19 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05), and the reason it is tracked: this is the LAST NATIONAL CPI READING THE BANK OF JAPAN HOLDS when it decides on 2027-03-18 (boj-decision-2027-03-18, estimate). That matters because it is the number that measures how much the March MPM's one-day miss of the February print (japan-cpi-2027-03-19, estimate) actually costs. The japan-cpi-2027-03-19 ledger benchmarked it: across 27 Februaries (2000-2026, e-Stat 2025-base files parsed locally), the national January core y/y sits 0.178pp mean absolute and 0.116pp median from the national February core y/y it precedes, against a Bureau that publishes to one decimal — so on the median February this print rounds to the one the board 'misses'. The same benchmark found that the Tokyo February flash (japan-cpi-tokyo-flash-2027-02-26, estimate), released a week after this print, beats it as an estimate of national February core in only 9 of those 27 years. That is the finding: THIS print, not the flash, is the better free estimate of the print the BoJ does not get. Impact is LOW for the same reason every Japanese CPI entry on this calendar is: no house playbook is keyed to Japanese prices, symbols is empty, and the value here is corridor structure and calibration rather than a price channel. Nothing tracked on this calendar sat anywhere in February 2027 before this entry. ASSESSED 2026-09-05 by this event's own initial research (docs/research/events/japan-cpi-2027-02-19.md), which re-fetched and re-parsed every primary independently and reached four findings. (1) The claim above HOLDS AND IS STRONGER AT JANUARY THAN THE SIBLING PROVED IT AT FEBRUARY: pointing the same persistence benchmark at January prints, the Tokyo flash loses in BOTH windows — Januaries 2000-2026 (n=27) 0.273pp vs 0.166pp, Tokyo wins 33%; Januaries 2018-2026 (n=9) 0.205pp vs 0.217pp, Tokyo wins 44%, the only sub-coin-flip 2018+ cell in the matrix, so the flash's one defence (it wins post-2018) does not exist here. (2) This session's own opening hypothesis was REFUTED: ranked against all twelve calendar months on mean absolute change in national core y/y from the prior month, January is rank 7 of 12 (0.166pp) on both samples, below the all-month mean of 0.182pp — there is no New-Year-reset effect and this print carries an ordinary amount of new information. (3) NEW FINDING, the most valuable one: the sole break in Japanese core persistence is APRIL — March-to-April is 0.366pp, rank 1 of 12 on both samples, 1.8x the second-worst month and 2.0x the all-month average, against eleven months packed into 0.125-0.204pp. Every 'the stale print is nearly as good' argument in this corridor is sound up to the April boundary and unsupported across it, which is where japan-food-tax-cut-2027-04-01 (-1.19pp on core) and boj-decision-2027-04-28 sit; flagged to those lanes, deliberately NOT registered as a forward test because the 2027 instance is confounded by the tax cut. (4) DATE CONFIDENCE is higher here than at the sibling: the published table spans 15 survey months so three appear twice, and the year-over-year drift is 1 day (Dec data, Fri->Fri), 1 day (THIS row, 2026-02-20 Fri -> 2027-02-19 Fri) and 5 days (Feb data, Tue->Fri) — this row has an observed precedent that held, and the Cabinet Office CSV shows February 2027's only two holidays fall Thursday (02-11) and Tuesday (02-23), so the Friday-holiday mechanism that moved the March row cannot reach this one. Two US-side events sharing this corridor were found unfiled and are proposed in the same PR: opex-2027-02-19 (Cboe lists VA/G7 settling 2027-02-19 directly, and VX/F7 2027-01-20 +30d reaches it independently) and vix-expiration-2027-02-17 (VX/G7 listed). The BoJ context is now measured rather than asserted: 2027 MPMs end Jan 22 / Mar 18 / Apr 28 / Jun 11 / Jul 22 / Sep 22 / Oct 29 / Dec 17, so this is the ONLY national CPI release inside the 55-day Jan-to-Mar gap (the second-longest of 2027, not the longest), and the Bank's sole scheduled February document is the January-MPM Summary of Opinions on 2027-02-01. Stance: stand aside, unchanged. FT-japan-cpi-2027-02-19-1/-2/-3 registered.
